cap: GH is released in pulses, so a single GH value is uninformative; IGF-1 from the liver integrates those pulses and is the screening test. Glucose normally suppresses GH, so a GH level that stays high after an oral glucose load confirms acromegaly. Surgery removes the adenoma, octreotide mimics somatostatin at the tumor, and pegvisomant blocks the GH receptor downstream.
teach: Pegvisomant is the odd one out: because it blocks the receptor rather than the secretion, IGF-1 falls while serum GH stays high or rises, so IGF-1, not GH, is the number used to adjust the dose. Octreotide also inhibits gallbladder contraction, which is why gallstones are its signature adverse effect.
